notes.title: 📢IMPORTANT MESSAGE
notes.notes: [p]In the past days, many players have contacted me saying their Steam accounts were compromised. Hackers are using those stolen accounts to buy Legend of Himari items on the Steam Community Market for absurdly high prices.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32277416/9e4984cb2b19e4eb03a1a7b834e25be10f05ef39.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32277416/675e486fdbade777e894ce726ecb2f395e64157f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]These are player-to-player transactions. The money goes from one user’s wallet to another, not to me as the developer. That means I cannot refund or reverse them — I have no access to those transactions.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32277416/cb0763cba0a3d27451db824106460f36a52c78a6.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Unfortunately, Steam support often redirects players back to [b]ME[/b], even though I have no tools to fix Community Market trades. I can only refund in-game purchases, not market deals between players.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32277416/fde9a97073ee8a3cd18e046034350d285b9b9e79.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]All items in [b]Legend of Himari[/b] drop just by playing the game. I don’t sell them directly - they are earned in-game. If you see them on the Steam Community Market, that’s purely players trading with each other, not me selling.[/p][p]I can remove items from a player’s inventory, but only if I already know their [b]SteamID[/b] and the exact item ID. But [b]I cannot see who is selling items on the Steam Market[/b]. [b]Steam does not share seller information with developers[/b].[/p][p]I [b]cannot ban someone from using the Steam Market[/b]. [b]Only Valve[/b] controls trading and the Community Market. I cannot cancel or refund a transaction once an item is sold on the Market — that is fully handled by Valve.[/p][p]It is almost impossible for me to track down which specific player is listing items for sale, since Steam hides that data.[/p][p]I can manage items [b]inside the game[/b], but I have no control over what happens on the Steam Market.[/p][p]At this moment, Valve hasn’t taken action to stop this issue or provide developers with a way to protect players from such scams. For example, I would like to set a maximum price for my items on the trading platform, but I am unable to do so at present.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32277416/53d40c867e7189cc2c41c10ea2f8c400c4f6bd13.png"][/img][/p][p]Also one obvious fix would be for Valve to remove the option to buy items at custom prices. Players should only be able to purchase the cheapest available listing. That alone would close the loophole hackers are exploiting.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32277416/a6e19b6a3a46bee4fd8f68b00cce14775cd581f1.png"][/img][/p][p]I’m very sorry my game is being misused like this. If this happens to you, please contact Steam Support and clearly state it was an unauthorized Community Market purchase.[/p][p]Also secure your account: change your password, enable Steam Guard, deauthorize devices, and revoke your API key.[/p]

notes.title: Four New Announcements
notes.notes:
My name is Ternox, and I’m an indie developer. Recently, I’ve also become an indie publisher of small games — mostly visual novels — as I run the Ukrainian Visual Novel Jam and look for interesting projects that could use some help with promotion.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/25363761/88a36b136b3516cbf8ce55cf6edc23fcdccd6fbb.jpg[/img]

Together with other developers, we’ve prepared four game announcements you can already add to your wishlist.

[h1]Valkyrie Iteration: Mecha Pilot Raising Pocket Simulator[/h1]
[b]Developer[/b]: TERNOX
[b]Art[/b]: Lumeish
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E6PSbDWXbXM
Valkyrie Iteration is a mini raising sim where you train Lana to battle mysterious phantoms — beings from another dimension tearing apart the fabric of reality.

To face this threat, humanity created Valkyries — giant combat mechs with souls of their own. These living machines have instincts and personalities, accepting only pilots capable of forming a deep emotional bond with them.

Plan Lana’s days, choose which stats to train, and hope she can make it to the finale without defeat.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3466240

[h1]Manic Pixie Dreamgirls[/h1]
[b]Developer[/b]: Kajan Collaboration
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QNpjwkGZYVU
A team of friends is creating a nostalgic visual novel inspired by early 2000s anime. Manic Pixie Dream Girls tells the story of half-fae students who enter their classmates’ dreams, influence their subconscious, and battle nightmares.

The style blends influences from Persona, Madoka Magica, and Tumblr-era aesthetics. Key moments present three choices, one of which always leads to a bad ending. Several artists and writers work on the project with the goal of recreating the vibe of eerie, old-school anime.

The visual novel was one of the winners of Ukrainian Visual Novel Jam #5 and is now being prepared for full release on Steam. You can already support the developers by adding it to your wishlist.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3828970

[h1]Born for the Light ~Wavelength Radiant Collapse~[/h1]
[b]Developer[/b]: qDrot
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VPv7onYDmVs

Solo developer qDrot is working on Born for the Light ~Wavelength Radiant Collapse~.

According to the developer, the project defies conventional expectations, exploring themes of religious trauma and illusions through the eyes of the protagonist.

The story unfolds in a world where children live high above the earth, inside a giant Tree, believing that one day they will fly to a distant Kingdom. The narrative leaves many questions unanswered, inviting players to search for meaning themselves.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3776830/

[h1]Desktop Akari ~my cute companion~[/h1]
[b]Developer[/b]: TERNOX
[b]Art[/b]: Phantom__651
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DH0RvraByjs
Remember “desktop companions” from the 2000s — when a little character would walk around your screen, sit on window edges, or perch on the Start bar? I decided to bring that idea back, but turn it into a full-fledged game — a quirky mix of idle game, raising sim, virtual friend, and even a touch of dating sim.

The main heroine is Akari from my visual novel PockeDate!, now ready to live right on your desktop. You’ll manage her schedule, give her tasks, help her study, socialize, and build her singing career, while also taking care of her mood and rest.

Desktop Akari will run over everything you do, not in a separate window, so she’ll always be there. Release is planned for early next year.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3702590

notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

As you already know, I intend to support the game and bring more content.

First of all, I want to add more rewards for passing and the opportunity to spend the accumulated stars on something useful or just pleasant.

In this regard, I had a desire to add new Steam achievements to the game, but I'm not sure how good this idea is for the community, because surely many people want to see the game 100% completed, and new achievements will make them return to the game.

Therefore, I will ask you: how do you feel about the emergence of new achievements? Would you mind that? Or is it better to leave them as they are?

notes.notes:
[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25363761/02592ac56fab21f3686b5c2c9deb0925525258ea.jpg[/img]
On December 16, 2015 I released my first commercial game - [b]Taimumari[/b]. It was not a perfect and polished game, but it was my dream. With Taimumari I was able to leave my office work and realize my projects.

And today, five years later, the game gets a major upgrade, straight from the consoles. I hope you will be pleased with the new graphics in the dialogues. If you wish, you can also play the classic version. https://store.steampowered.com/app/375520
The new Definitive Edition also includes an addition with Kanashimi, which now does not need to be purchased separately.

I am also developing Taimumari 2 and unfortunately I was not able to release it by the fifth anniversary as planned. There's still a lot of work to do, so I don't know when I can release it yet. https://store.steampowered.com/app/1292400
However, my small BakuMari project will be released soon - you can check out its Steam page now. https://store.steampowered.com/app/1470880/BakuMari
I appreciate your support and hope that you will also play my future games. [b]Thank you all![/b]

notes.title: NEXORIA
notes.notes:
Legend of Himari 2 change title to NEXORIA. After all, the arcade game turned into a tactical turn-based dungeon-crowler game. The game has become so unlike "Legend of Himari" that I decided to untie this game from any franchise and make it an independent product. But still in the Taimumari universe.

Moreover, the game will be released on February 18, but only in early access. Active participation of Steam player community is necessary for creating a quality game.

So, NEXORIA — is a hardcore roguelike about dungeons with hybrid battles, combining classical turn based combat system and a collectible card game. Collect the best spells and conquer the dungeons!

This game is a unique mix of rogue-like with dungeon exploration, RPG, turn-based tactics and collectible card game. At the base of the turn-based system are not turns, but time. Find and improve new heroes and get coins to buy new spells. But remember, a hero’s death will be fatal.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/932210/NEXORIA/
